clue.text: The academic field

parts.note: the grounds of a university are the field where academic life happens; the word is also Latin for a field

explanation.definitionFit: A university's grounds, its buildings and lawns, are literally the field that belongs to the academics.

clue.text: Gun-support bearing

definitions.meaning: the wheeled frame on which a field gun is mounted
the way a person holds and carries themself, their posture

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the wheeled mount for a cannon and a person's deportment or posture.

clue.text: French husband has a period by the sea

parts.note: mari is the French word for husband
a period is a stretch of time

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's husband spends a spell at the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: Maritime describes things connected with or lying beside the sea, such as coastal provinces.

clue.text: This description is hardly fair comment

definitions.text: This description is hardly fair comment

parts.words: This description is hardly fair comment
parts.note: read 'fair' as good-looking, not just: a remark calling someone the opposite of fair-faced

explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone unattractive is the opposite of saying they are fair, meaning pretty.

clue.text: I'm engaged in property valuation

indicators.note: being engaged in something means being occupied within it, so these letters go inside the property

parts.note: an estate is a large piece of landed property
taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone says they are busy with putting a price on a house.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimate is an approximate valuation, a rough reckoning of worth or cost.

clue.text: The pleasure of compensation

definitions.meaning: the contentment felt when a wish is met
amends made for a wrong, as in demanding redress

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both contentment from fulfilment and redress made for an injury or insult.

clue.text: Rain is unusual here

indicators.note: an unusual version of a word has its letters in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Rainfall is a rare event in this dry place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' points to the place the whole clue describes: a mostly arid country of the Middle East where rain is indeed scarce.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue paints a dry land, and this Middle Eastern nation is largely desert, so it is the place meant.

clue.text: About to happen soon in the vicinity

definitions.meaning: imminent, as when an event is near in time

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means nearby, either in time (imminent) or in space (within reach).

clue.text: One of two that is set up to the right

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means written upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
taken as written

explanation.surface: One of a pair that has been arranged on the right-hand side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' signals a reversal because in a down light the letters are written upwards; 'to' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun means one or the other of a pair, as in 'take either'.

clue.text: Not often there's real trouble in the railway

indicators.note: one piece sits inside another, here within the railway abbreviation
real in trouble is upset and disordered, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Genuine trouble on the line is an infrequent event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' is the anagram signal and 'in' puts the shuffled word inside the railway abbreviation; the surface pictures a rail fault, not frequency.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarely means seldom, on few occasions.

clue.text: War that's breaking out in Panama?

indicators.note: breaking out suggests the letters burst loose and regroup in a new order

explanation.surface: Hostilities erupt in the Central American country.
explanation.walkthrough: Panama looks like the country but is a lightweight brimmed hat; the question mark marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Panama is a kind of lightweight woven brimmed hat, one example of a summer boater-style headwear.

clue.text: As set by one out to break a record?

definitions.text: As set by one out to break a record?

parts.words: As set by one out to break a record?
parts.note: a runner chasing a record sets a very fast speed; 'cracking' is also breaking, as a record might be cracked

explanation.definitionFit: A very fast speed is what an athlete attempting a record must establish.

clue.text: I return to a trivial item

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word to is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone goes back to a trifling object.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek letter's name is used for a tiny amount, a jot or whit.

clue.text: Split the pot

definitions.meaning: slang for inform on someone to the police

explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang both for betraying someone to the police and for marijuana.

clue.text: Born at the King's Head-a low joint

indicators.note: at here places one piece next to the other, the king's letter going in front
the head of a word is its first letter, here taken from King's

parts.note: née, used of a woman's maiden name, means born

explanation.surface: Someone was born in a pub called the King's Head, a seedy dive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a low joint' looks like a dingy bar, matching the pub; it is a body joint low down on the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is a joint in the lower part of the leg.

clue.text: Humphrey's artless look to us appears phoney

indicators.note: artless literally means without art, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Humphrey Bogart was the Hollywood star of Casablanca
taken as written

explanation.surface: The film star's naive expression towards us seems fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look to' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogus means fake or counterfeit, not genuine.

clue.text: Possibly Indian form of canoe

indicators.note: a form of a word is a reshaping of it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Perhaps a native American style of boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' suggests a Native American canoe, but it is the Indian Ocean, one example of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian is one of the world's great oceans, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: You'll be lucky to win one

definitions.text: You'll be lucky to win one

parts.words: You'll be lucky to win one
parts.note: a contest decided by luck rather than skill, which only the fortunate win

explanation.definitionFit: A contest such as roulette or dice is won purely by luck, so only a lucky player wins it.

clue.text: The adder is squirming when strung up

indicators.note: a squirming snake wriggles out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A snake writhes as it is hanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Beads are threaded when they are strung up on a cord.

clue.text: I forsake the Law for the Artillery

indicators.note: to forsake is to abandon, so the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: an ordinance is a decree or local law
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man quits legal practice to join the gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance means military guns and artillery collectively.

clue.text: One whose pupils are told to make notes

definitions.text: One whose pupils are told to make notes

parts.words: One whose pupils are told to make notes
parts.note: not a classroom teacher dictating, but one whose students produce musical sounds

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who instructs students in playing an instrument or singing gets them to produce musical sounds.

clue.text: One who's learned to park a vehicle in the street

indicators.note: parking something in the street puts it inside the street's abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written
a van is a goods vehicle

explanation.surface: A man has learnt how to leave his car by the roadside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One who's learned' reads as someone who has just picked up a skill; it means a scholar, learned as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A savant is a scholar, someone of great learning.

clue.text: PC Skinner

definitions.meaning: a police constable; old British slang named police after Sir Robert Peel
something or someone that removes skins, as from fruit

explanation.definitionFit: Old British slang for a police officer, after Robert Peel, is also a tool that strips rind from potatoes.

clue.text: Tree, one found by the river

parts.note: an ace is the one in a suit of cards

explanation.surface: A tree is discovered beside the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is the botanical name for the maple genus of trees.

clue.text: I pick up key to look round Inuit house

parts.note: G is one of the musical keys
lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone collects a key in order to look around an Arctic dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a domed snow shelter built by the Inuit.

clue.text: Forest's administrative fellow

definitions.meaning: the Forest of ... is an ancient woodland in Gloucestershire, England
a senior college official who runs discipline or a faculty

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a Gloucestershire forest and a college or cathedral official.

clue.text: Singer has altered a lot

indicators.note: altered means changed, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A vocalist has changed a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with a voice in the low female or high male range.

clue.text: Twisted wire could be a danger to riverboats

definitions.text: could be a danger to riverboats

indicators.note: twisted wire is bent out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bent cable might be a hazard for boats on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a low dam across a river, which boats must avoid.
explanation.definitionFit: A weir is a low dam across a river, hazardous to boats approaching its drop.

clue.text: It's heard after the raid that nobody is found guilty

definitions.meaning: the siren sounded in wartime once an air attack was over
a verdict or finding that everyone is cleared

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the siren after an air raid ends, and a finding that all suspects are exonerated.

clue.text: Not how Anne Boleyn's ghost will collide with you

definitions.text: Not how Anne Boleyn's ghost will collide with you

parts.words: Not how Anne Boleyn's ghost will collide with you
parts.note: the beheaded queen's ghost is said to carry her severed head under her arm, so she cannot meet you face first

explanation.walkthrough: Anne Boleyn, a wife of Henry VIII, was beheaded; her ghost is pictured carrying her head.
explanation.definitionFit: A head-first, face-to-face collision is impossible for a ghost whose head is tucked under her arm.

clue.text: Pass on the takings

definitions.meaning: to hand over, as a suspect to the police
the total sales revenue of a business

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means hand over; as one it is a business's gross revenue.

clue.text: Game couple

definitions.meaning: a card game for four players in partnerships
to join or connect two things, as a span joins two banks

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a partnership card game and a structure that joins two sides together.
